name: Street Review: rating Montréal streets for inclusivity, aesthetics, practicality and accessibility
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (60 new Montréal street locations from Google Street View, captured 2018–2026, © Google, each shown as two views looking in opposite directions as in the paper). Based on Mushkani & Koseki, "Street Review: A participatory AI-based framework for assessing streetscape inclusivity" (Cities 170, 2026, 106602; arXiv:2508.11708). Participants first give age group, gender, mobility limitation and LGBTQ2+ identity (each with "prefer not to say"), the groups the paper compared. They then rate 20 locations, each shown as two opposite-direction images, on the paper's four criteria: inclusivity, aesthetics, practicality and accessibility, on a 1–4 scale with the paper's Table 2 wording for every score (e.g. 1 = "Not inclusive or welcoming", 4 = "Fully inclusive and welcoming to all"). In the paper, 12 residents (out of 28 interviewed) each rated 60 locations on 20 streets in focus groups, and scores averaged per demographic group trained models applied to about 45,000 Mapillary images.

Differences from the original study: (1) the 60 locations are random Street View points in Montréal, not head/centre/tail points on 20 streets chosen for density, income, greenery and history; (2) each participant rates a random 20 of the 60 locations instead of all 60; (3) online and individual only, without the paper's interviews, group discussion, collective rating and ranking; (4) the paper does not give its question wording for the background questions; these are our wording of the groups the paper used.
author: Mushkani & Koseki
